item.title: The sentence demanded in the case of jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu is 2,430 years
item.description: The opposition Republican People's Party (CHP), which İmamoğlu represents, has condemned the case as politically driven — arguing the timing and scope are aimed at sidelining a major political opponent.

item.title: Participatory monitoring breathes life into Cameroon’s Marine Protected Area
item.description: The marine protected area faces several challenges — ones that the local communities are working hard to mitigate through participatory monitoring. Yet the protected area continues to face threats.

item.title: Queer cinema in Azerbaijan tells stories of visibility and survival
item.description: These films transform personal struggles into collective narratives, illustrating how survival, memory, and the quest for belonging are intertwined with the creation of queer cinematic histories.

item.title: Exploring China’s growing role in Central Asia
item.description: “All five Central Asian landlocked states were particularly focused on turning the limitations of being “landlocked” into advantages of being “landlinked”; to be an inseparable part of global connectivity networks and beneficiaries of them.”

item.title: When the judge meets the algorithm: AI tools entering India’s courts
item.description: Indian courts are adopting AI and emerging technologies to tackle backlogs and bureaucracy, yet success depends on addressing ethical safeguards and effectively training judges and citizens for responsible implementation.

item.title: ’I don't see Palestine as an isolated story‘: An interview with Vivien Sansour, founder of the Palestine Heirloom Seed Library
item.description: “[W]e want the Seed Library to be a place of freedom, an initiative for us to have autonomy over our food, but also over our spirit, our minds, our words.”

item.title: Indonesian journalists seek better pay and protection amid declining democracy
item.description: Indonesian journalists demand better pay and protection of their rights amid a changing media landscape and restrictions on civic space

item.title: In the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, mining revenue is helping to fund rebel groups
item.description: The security crisis in eastern DRC is escalating after two rebel groups, both fighting the government, joined forces.

item.title: Georgia marks a year of protests
item.description: Despite declining numbers, hundreds — sometimes thousands — continue to protest daily. The duration of the movement remains uncertain, but the government’s shift toward authoritarianism appears unmistakable.

item.title: ‘Identity is never fixed. It’s layered, constantly shifting’: An interview with Iranian-American artist Soraya Sharghi
item.description: “My way of resisting is through creating by bringing beauty, strength, and imagination into spaces where control or limitation once existed.”
